title: Matter and the Atom: An Introduction to Chemistry

questions.question: Which subatomic particle determines the identity of an element?
questions.rationale: The atomic number — the proton count — defines the element. Neutrons vary among isotopes; electrons balance charge.

questions.question: A neutral sodium atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons does it contain?
Table salt (NaCl) is best classified as:
questions.rationale: Sodium and chlorine are chemically bonded in a fixed 1:1 ratio — a compound whose properties differ completely from its elements.

questions.question: Burning paper produces ash, carbon dioxide, and water vapour. This is a:
options: Physical change, because energy is released
Physical change, because the paper gets smaller
Chemical change, because new substances form
questions.rationale: The test is identity: new substances with new properties mean a chemical change.

questions.question: An ionic bond forms when:
options: Electrons are transferred between metal and non-metal atoms
Free electrons flow around positive ions
questions.rationale: Ionic bonding is electron transfer (e.g. Na → Cl); sharing is covalent; the mobile electron sea is metallic bonding.

questions.question: Which state of matter has a fixed volume but no fixed shape, with flowing particles?
questions.rationale: Liquids keep their volume but take the container's shape — particles flow. Solids have fixed shape; gases have neither fixed shape nor volume.

questions.question: The change from gas to liquid, releasing heat, is called:
questions.rationale: Condensation is gas → liquid with heat released (heat out). Evaporation and melting take heat in.

questions.question: Carbon-12 and carbon-14 differ in which respect?
questions.rationale: Isotopes are atoms of one element differing only in neutron count; the proton count (and thus the element) stays the same.

questions.question: A neutral atom has atomic number 11. How many electrons does it contain?
questions.rationale: In a neutral atom, electron count balances the proton count: atomic number 11 → 11 protons → 11 electrons.

questions.question: Water and carbon dioxide are compounds because they:
options: Contain two or more elements chemically bonded in fixed ratios
Contain only one type of atom
Can exist as gas, liquid, or solid
questions.rationale: Compounds have two or more elements chemically bonded in fixed ratios (H₂O, CO₂), with properties utterly different from their component elements.

questions.question: Which bond type explains why metals conduct electricity well?
options: Metallic bonds — an electron 'sea' around positive ions
questions.rationale: In metallic bonding, mobile free electrons form a 'sea' around positive ions, letting charge flow — that's what makes metals conductive.
